message_source_quote: **Novelty**: distinct from WBS (Raman et al.) — own prompts, own concepts, own carrier sentences, independently captured and calibrated.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a stance direction from WSB's `directed_modulation` family lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 on the 4B. We do not reproduce that method: we write our own contrastive prompts with different concepts and carrier sentences, capture residuals independently, and find our own dose.

(2026) / the white-bear steering (WBS) work as the prior method the stance-contrast direction is in the same family as, and both explicitly claim the submitted method does not reproduce it but instead uses independently written prompts, concepts, carrier sentences, captured residuals and a separately calibrated dose/scale. The message's shorthand 'WBS (Raman et al.)' and the write-up's 'Raman et al. (2026)' / 'WSB's directed_modulation family' refer to the same source and benchmark bank without contradiction, so there is no material difference in naming, overlap, or novelty framing between the two documents.
